asks.plainAsk: Ask for a written warning and time to pay before a late payment counts as breaking the lease.
asks.legalWording: Tenant shall not be in default for failure to pay Rent unless such failure continues for [ten (10)] days after written notice from Landlord.

asks.plainAsk: Ask to get a written warning every time, not just the first few times.
asks.legalWording: Landlord shall give Tenant written notice of each failure to pay Rent before such failure becomes an Event of Default.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the lease's warning come on top of any warning the law gives you, not replace it.
asks.legalWording: Any notice under this Section shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, any notice required by law.

asks.plainAsk: Ask to cap your personal guaranty at a set amount, or have it end after the business pays on time for a set period.
asks.legalWording: Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Guarantor's liability under this Guaranty shall not exceed [$amount].

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the landlord try to collect from the business before coming to you.
asks.legalWording: Landlord shall first exhaust its remedies against Tenant before seeking payment from Guarantor.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that your guaranty not cover renewals or changes you didn't agree to in writing.
asks.legalWording: Guarantor shall not be liable for any renewal, extension, or amendment of the Lease unless Guarantor consents to it in writing.

asks.plainAsk: Ask to pay only increases above a starting year, or for a limit on yearly increases.
asks.legalWording: Tenant shall pay Tenant's Proportionate Share of the amount by which Operating Expenses for each year exceed Operating Expenses for the Base Year.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that major building upgrades, like a new roof, be left out of your share.
asks.legalWording: Operating Expenses shall not include the cost of capital improvements, capital repairs, or capital replacements.

asks.plainAsk: Ask for a limit on how far the real amount can go above the estimate, and the right to see the landlord's records.
asks.legalWording: Tenant's share of Operating Expenses for the first Lease Year shall not exceed [110%] of the estimate in this Lease. Tenant may inspect Landlord's records of Operating Expenses on reasonable notice.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the yearly limit not carry forward, so a slow year doesn't allow a bigger increase later.
asks.legalWording: The limit on increases in Controllable Operating Expenses shall apply each year without carry-forward of any unused amount.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the landlord need a good reason to refuse.
asks.legalWording: Landlord's consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that selling your business, or bringing in a partner, not need the landlord's permission.
asks.legalWording: A transfer of ownership interests in Tenant shall not be deemed an assignment of this Lease.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the landlord not be able to take the space back when you ask to transfer the lease.
asks.legalWording: Landlord shall have no right to terminate this Lease in connection with any proposed assignment or sublease.

asks.plainAsk: Ask to be released once the landlord approves the buyer.
asks.legalWording: Upon any assignment approved by Landlord, Tenant and any Guarantor shall be released from all obligations arising after the date of the assignment.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the landlord need your agreement to move you, or at least pay for the move and finish the new space first.
asks.legalWording: Landlord shall not relocate Tenant without Tenant's prior written consent.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the landlord pay all moving costs and finish the new space before you move.
asks.legalWording: Landlord shall pay all of Tenant's reasonable costs of relocating, and Tenant shall not be required to move until the substitute premises are complete.

asks.plainAsk: Ask to remove the landlord's right to end early, or for more notice and repayment of what you spent on the space.
asks.legalWording: If Landlord terminates this Lease under this Section, Landlord shall give at least [twelve (12) months'] notice and pay Tenant the unamortized cost of Tenant's improvements to the Premises.

asks.plainAsk: Ask for more time to refill the deposit.
asks.legalWording: within [thirty (30)] days after written demand

asks.plainAsk: Ask for a rent reduction if a service is out for more than a few days for reasons the landlord controls.
asks.legalWording: If any utility or service is interrupted for more than [three (3)] consecutive business days for reasons within Landlord's reasonable control, Rent shall abate until service is restored.

asks.plainAsk: Ask for a rent reduction if a service is out for more than a few days.
asks.legalWording: If any utility or service is interrupted for more than [three (3)] consecutive business days, Rent shall abate until service is restored.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that you only have to remove changes the landlord names in writing when it approves them.
asks.legalWording: Tenant shall have no obligation to remove any improvements except those Landlord designates in writing at the time it approves them.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that rent stop while the space is unusable, and that you can end the lease if repairs take too long.
asks.legalWording: Rent shall abate while the Premises are untenantable. If the Premises are not restored within [180] days after the casualty, Tenant may terminate this Lease.

asks.plainAsk: Ask that the landlord's lender promise to keep your lease if it takes over the building.
asks.legalWording: Tenant's subordination is conditioned on Tenant receiving a non-disturbance agreement from each holder of a mortgage on the Building.

asks.plainAsk: Ask for a way to end the lease early, for example after a set year with notice and a fee.
asks.legalWording: Tenant may terminate this Lease effective at the end of the [third] Lease Year by giving at least [six (6)] months' written notice and paying a termination fee of [$amount].
